Population-averaged score probabilities, expected scores and exceedance

Source: R/marginal.R
brs_marginal.Rd

Score distribution of a brs or brsmm fit at given covariate values, with standard errors and intervals: the probabilities \(P(S = s)\) of the scores \(0, \ldots, K\), the expected score or the exceedance probabilities \(P(S \ge k)\), and differences of these between pairs of rows. For brsmm fits the random effects are integrated out (marginal, population-averaged quantities) or set to zero (conditional = TRUE).

Usage

brs_marginal(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("prob", "expected_score", "exceed"),
  k = NULL,
  contrast = NULL,
  conditional = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  se_method = c("delta", "simulation"),
  n_sim = 1000L,
  n_points = 8L
)

Arguments

object

A fitted "brs" or "brsmm" object.

newdata

Data frame of covariate values, one prediction per row; NULL (default) uses the rows of the fit.

type

"prob" (default; probabilities of the scores \(0, \ldots, K\)), "expected_score" or "exceed".

k

Integer thresholds in \(0, \ldots, K\) for type = "exceed"; NULL (default) uses \(1, \ldots, K\).

contrast

Optional pairs of rows of newdata to compare: a two-column matrix with one pair per row, a list of length-2 vectors, or a single length-2 vector. The pair c(i, j) gives the quantity of row i minus that of row j.

conditional

Logical; TRUE sets the random effects to zero instead of integrating them out (no effect for brs fits).

level

Confidence level of the intervals (default 0.95).

se_method

"delta" (default) or "simulation".

n_sim

Number of parameter draws for se_method = "simulation" (default 1000).

n_points

Gauss-Legendre nodes per panel of the random-effect integral (default 8; see Details).

Value

A data frame of class "brs_marginal" with the columns of newdata (or, for contrasts, contrast, row1 and row2), row, score (type = "prob") or k (type = "exceed"), estimate, std.error, lower and upper. Attributes: type, conditional, level, se_method, n_nodes (total quadrature nodes; NA without random effects) and, for the delta method, jacobian (quantities by parameters).

Details

For a row with fixed-effect linear predictor \(\eta\) and random-effect design \(x_r\), the marginal score probabilities are $$P(S = s) = \int P(S = s \mid \eta + x_r^\top b)\, \varphi(b; 0, D)\, db = E\{P(S = s \mid \eta + u)\}, \qquad u \sim N(0, x_r^\top D x_r),$$ because \(b\) enters the model only through \(u = x_r^\top b\) (the dispersion submodel has no random effects), so the integral is one-dimensional whatever the number of random effects. It is computed on \(z = u / \mathrm{SD}(u) \in [-8.5, 8.5]\) by a composite Gauss-Legendre rule with n_points nodes per panel and panels of width at most 1 on the scale of \(z\) and at most 0.5 on the scale of \(u\) (the conditional probabilities can change quickly with \(u\) when the precision is high or the variance large, where Gauss-Hermite rules converge slowly). A warning is given when halving the panel width changes a value by more than \(10^{-6}\).

\(P(S = s \mid \cdot)\) is the probability of the cell of \(s\) under the latent beta law, with the cells of the fit's interval map or its estimated boundary cutpoints (as in brs_predict_scoreprob, but without a probability floor), so each row sums to 1 whenever the cells partition (0, 1) (lim = 0.5, or interval = "right" or "left"). "expected_score" is \(\sum_s s\, P(S = s)\) on the \(0, \ldots, K\) scale and "exceed" is \(P(S \ge k) = \sum_{s \ge k} P(S = s)\). When the cells do not partition (0, 1) (interval = "mid" with lim < 0.5), the probabilities sum to less than 1 and these two types are not moments or tail probabilities of a distribution; they are computed with a warning.

Under a nonlinear link the marginal quantities differ from the conditional ones at \(b = 0\): the latter describe a subject whose random effects are zero, not the population average, and the gap grows with the random-effect variance. For a brs fit both coincide.

Uncertainty: with se_method = "delta" (default), delta-method standard errors from a Richardson central-difference Jacobian of the quantities in all parameters of coef(object) (regression, precision, random-effect Cholesky and boundary-cutpoint parameters) and vcov(object). The Wald intervals are computed on the logit scale for probabilities and for \(E[S]/K\) and transformed back (so they stay in range), and on the natural scale for contrasts. With se_method = "simulation", n_sim parameter vectors are drawn from \(N(\hat\theta, V)\); the standard error is the standard deviation of the quantity over the draws and the interval its percentile interval (the draws use the RNG: call set.seed() first for reproducible values). The estimate is always the plug-in value at \(\hat\theta\).

Rows of newdata with missing covariates give NA; the response and the grouping variable are not needed.

See also

brsmm, brs_predict_scoreprob, predict.brsmm, brs_loglik_contrib

Examples

# Synthetic NRS-11 scores of 40 patients at three times. Simulated data.
set.seed(21)
nrs <- expand.grid(id = 1:40, time = c("6h", "12h", "24h"))
b0 <- rnorm(40, sd = 0.8)
eta <- -1.3 + c(0, 0.75, 0.3)[nrs$time] + b0[nrs$id]
shp <- brs_repar(mu = plogis(eta), phi = 0.2, repar = 2)
nrs$y <- round(10 * rbeta(nrow(nrs), shp$shape1, shp$shape2))
m <- brsmm(y ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, data = nrs, ncuts = 10)

nd <- data.frame(time = c("6h", "12h", "24h"))
# Population-averaged mean score and P(S >= 4) at each time
brs_marginal(m, nd, type = "expected_score")
#>   time row estimate std.error    lower    upper
#> 1   6h   1 2.765695 0.3641912 2.111009 3.532504
#> 2  12h   2 3.851484 0.4053013 3.093410 4.669726
#> 3  24h   3 3.270770 0.3888986 2.558315 4.073039
brs_marginal(m, nd, type = "exceed", k = 4)
#>   time row k  estimate  std.error     lower     upper
#> 1   6h   1 4 0.3343304 0.05886990 0.2302121 0.4575490
#> 2  12h   2 4 0.5081511 0.06331141 0.3860665 0.6292713
#> 3  24h   3 4 0.4157591 0.06246982 0.3006362 0.5408725
# Same at b = 0 (a typical patient): not the population average
brs_marginal(m, nd, type = "expected_score", conditional = TRUE)
#>   time row estimate std.error    lower    upper
#> 1   6h   1 2.505481 0.3874073 1.824161 3.337397
#> 2  12h   2 3.693577 0.4560510 2.852212 4.622623
#> 3  24h   3 3.050062 0.4262105 2.283504 3.942475
# Change from 6h: 12h - 6h and 24h - 6h
brs_marginal(m, nd, type = "expected_score",
             contrast = rbind(c(2, 1), c(3, 1)))
#>   contrast row1 row2  estimate std.error      lower    upper
#> 1    2 - 1    2    1 1.0857891 0.4060157  0.2900130 1.881565
#> 2    3 - 1    3    1 0.5050746 0.3970664 -0.2731613 1.283311
